title: Fencing the biggest pen
line: A rectangle of 40 m fence slides its width from 1 to 19 while the area counter climbs, peaks at 100, then falls.

title: The cheapest soup can
line: A can holding 500 cm³ morphs from tall and skinny to short and wide as a metal-used graph dips to its lowest point.

title: The lifeguard's fastest path
line: A lifeguard runs on sand then swims; the water entry point slides along the shore until the time readout bottoms out.

title: A page grid from squares
line: A page rectangle keeps snipping off squares, each leftover a smaller copy of the page, while the side ratio settles at 1.618.

title: Same crowd, smaller town
line: 100 dots spread over a 10×10 grid squeeze into a 5×5 corner and the people-per-square counter jumps from 1 to 4.

title: Pepperoni per square inch
line: A 10-inch and a 14-inch pizza each get 20 pepperonis, and the bigger pizza's toppings-per-square-inch readout drops to about half.

title: Measuring a lake with circles
line: A wobbly lake outline gets covered by three circles whose areas add up, then the estimate is compared with a grid-square count.

title: A person made of rectangles
line: A stick-figure outline fills in with a circle head and rectangle torso and limbs, each labeled, while a total area counter adds up.

title: Slicing a cone sideways
line: A knife line tilts through a cone drawn from the side while the slice beside it morphs from circle to ellipse to parabola.

title: Spinning a semicircle into a ball
line: A semicircle flips around its diameter like a spinning coin, squashing and stretching, and its ghost copies pile up into a sphere's outline.

title: A hexagon hiding in a cube
line: A slicing plane tilts through a cube and the cut face changes from triangle to square to a perfect hexagon.

title: Three cones fill a can
line: A cone-shaped cup pours sand into a cylinder of matching height and radius, filling it exactly after three pours.

title: A ball in a tin can
line: A ball of radius 3 drops into a snug can full of water; the water spills, leaving 18π of the can's 54π behind.

title: Double the cone
line: A cone's radius doubles and its volume counter jumps 4×, then its height doubles and the counter jumps 2× more.

title: Shoving a stack of coins
line: A neat stack of 12 coins gets pushed into a leaning tower, and the volume counter never changes as each coin slides.

title: Hemisphere slices match rings
line: A slice line rises through a hemisphere and a cone-hollowed cylinder, and the disk and ring slices always have equal areas.

title: Sliding strips of a triangle
line: A triangle cut into 10 thin horizontal strips gets sheared sideways strip by strip, and its area stays 12 the whole time.

title: Pizza into a rectangle
line: A circle of radius 2 splits into 16 slices that unzip and interlock into a near-rectangle measuring πr by r.

title: Rolling out pi
line: A circle with diameter 1 rolls one full turn along a number line, its rim peeling off flat to land past 3.14.

title: Onion rings into a triangle
line: A disk made of 20 thin rings has each ring snipped and straightened, stacking into a triangle with base 2πr and height r.

title: Perimeter with hidden staircases
line: Each side of a pentagon on a grid sprouts its right-triangle legs, its length gets computed, and the perimeter total adds up.

title: Box it and subtract
line: A triangle at (1,1), (6,2), (3,5) gets boxed in a 5×4 rectangle, three corner triangles peel off, and 20 drops to 9.

title: Lacing up the shoelace formula
line: A polygon's coordinates stack in a column, crossing arrows lace between them like shoelaces, and the products sum to twice the area.

title: Two-fifths of the way
line: A dot slides from (−4,−1) toward (6,4) with a ratio counter and stops at 2:3, landing exactly on (0,1).

title: Balancing the seesaw
line: Weights of 3 and 2 sit at a segment's ends, and a pivot slides until the bar levels at the 2:3 point.

title: Splitting the staircase
line: A segment's rise and run chop into 5 equal steps, and the partition point hops step by step to the second one.

title: Turning a slope sideways
line: A line with slope 2/3 and its rise-run triangle rotate 90°, the legs swap and one flips sign, and the slope reads −3/2.

title: The product stuck at −1
line: A line spins around the origin with a perpendicular partner; both slope readouts change wildly while their product stays at −1.

title: Sliding to the point
line: A line y = 2x − 3 slides upward, keeping its slope triangle, until it passes through (1,4), and its equation updates live.

title: Midpoints always make a parallelogram
line: A lopsided quadrilateral's corners wander around; joining its side midpoints always gives a parallelogram whose matching slope readouts stay equal.

title: The hypotenuse midpoint
line: A right triangle at (0,0), (2a,0), (0,2b) reshapes as a and b change; three distances from the hypotenuse midpoint stay equal.

title: String and two pins
line: A pencil pulls a string loop around two pins, tracing an ellipse while its two distances change but always sum to 10.

title: The difference stays 4
line: A dot traces both branches of a hyperbola as its distances to two foci change, but their difference readout never leaves 4.

title: Pulling a circle apart
line: Two foci start together at a circle's center and drift apart, squashing the circle into a flatter and flatter ellipse.

title: Equal distances make a parabola
line: A dot slides along a curve with segments to the focus (0,1) and the line y = −1, always equal.

title: Circles meet lines
line: Circles grow around the focus while matching horizontal lines rise, and each crossing drops a dot until a parabola appears.

title: Folding paper into a parabola
line: Fold lines appear one by one, each folding a directrix point onto the focus, and together they hug out a parabola.

title: Pythagoras sweeps a circle
line: A right triangle with hypotenuse 5 spins around (2,−1), its legs relabel as x−2 and y+1, and its tip traces a circle.

title: Completing the square with tiles
line: An x² tile and a 6x strip split into two 3x strips around the square, and a missing 3×3 corner tile completes it.

title: Twelve points at distance 5
line: Grid points at distance 5 from the origin light up, (3,4), (4,3), (5,0) and nine more, all on one circle.

title: Wrapping radii around a circle
line: A radius-length string bends onto the rim again and again; six fit with a sliver left over, and the counter reads 6.28.

title: Same angle, bigger arc
line: A 60° wedge cuts circles of radius 1, 2, and 3; their arc lengths count up while arc ÷ radius stays 1.047.

title: Growing a sector
line: An angle opens from 0 to 2π, the pie slice fills in, and its area counter tracks ½r²θ the whole way.

title: A circle finds the tangent
line: A circle drawn on OP as diameter crosses the original circle at two points, and lines from P through them just touch it.

title: Two crossings merge into one
line: A line from an outside point swings down, and its two crossing points on the circle slide together into one tangent point.

title: Two tangents, equal lengths
line: A point outside a circle wanders around while its two tangent segments are drawn, and their length readouts always match.

title: Growing the incircle
line: Three angle bisectors meet at a point, and a circle inflates from it until it kisses all three sides at once.

title: Chasing the circumcenter
line: Perpendicular bisectors meet and a circle passes through all three corners; dragging one vertex pushes the center outside an obtuse triangle.

title: Opposite angles add to 180
line: Four points slide around a circle; the quadrilateral's angles A and C keep changing, but their sum readout stays 180°.

title: The inscribed angle is half
line: A point slides around the circle's rim; its inscribed angle reads 35° everywhere while the central angle on the same arc stays 70°.

title: Right angles in a semicircle
line: A point slides along a semicircle, and the angle it makes with the diameter's ends stays locked at a right angle.

title: Crossing chords, equal products
line: Two chords cross inside a circle and wiggle; their pieces keep changing, but piece times piece on each chord always matches.

title: Slide and scale a circle
line: A circle of radius 1 slides onto a bigger circle's center and dilates by 3 until it fits exactly over it.

title: Shining a circle bigger
line: Rays from a point outside two circles pass through matching points, showing a single dilation carries the small circle onto the big one.

title: Measuring across a river
line: Two surveyors 50 m apart sight a tree across a river at 70° and 60°, the triangle closes, and the distance appears.

title: Opening a hinge
line: Sides of 5 and 7 hinge open from 0° to 180°, the third side grows from 2 to 12, passing √74 at 90°.

title: Two forces, one push
line: Arrows of 30 N and 40 N at 60° slide tip to tail, and the resultant arrow measures about 60.8 N.

title: Pythagoras with a correction
line: As angle C opens past 90°, the squares on a and b stop filling c's square, and a 2ab cos C strip appears.

title: One height, two ways
line: An altitude drops inside a triangle, labeled b sin A from one side and a sin B from the other: the law of sines.

title: The ratio that is the diameter
line: A triangle's vertices slide around a circle of radius 3 while a ÷ sin A stays fixed at 6, the diameter.

title: Tilting the side
line: Sides 6 and 4 meet at angle C, the dropped height 4 sin C grows and shrinks, and the area peaks at 12.

title: Two copies make a parallelogram
line: A triangle spins half a turn about a side's midpoint into a parallelogram of area ab sin C, twice the triangle.

title: How tall is the tree
line: A sightline from 20 m away tilts up 35° to a treetop, a right triangle fills in, and the height counts to 14 m.

title: The sliding ladder
line: A 5 m ladder slides down a wall; its base and height readouts trade off while base² plus height² stays 25.

title: Swapping the corners
line: A 30°-60°-90° triangle flips so its acute angles trade places, and the side labeled sin 30° becomes cos 60°.

title: Mirror across y = x
line: A point at angle θ on the unit circle reflects across y = x to angle 90° − θ, and its coordinates swap.

title: Same angle, same ratio
line: A 30° right triangle grows from tiny to huge, and its opposite ÷ hypotenuse counter never budges from 0.500.

title: A fan of 40° triangles
line: Five right triangles share one 40° corner, nested like a fan, and a table fills with the same 0.839 for every one.

title: Turning the angle dial
line: An angle slides from 0° to 90°, the triangle reshapes, and its opposite ÷ hypotenuse ratio climbs smoothly from 0 to 1.

title: A shadow measures the flagpole
line: A 2 m person's 3 m shadow triangle slides and scales onto a flagpole's 18 m shadow, showing the pole is 12 m.

title: A mirror on the floor
line: A light ray bounces off a floor mirror to your eye, making two similar triangles that reveal how tall the wall is.

title: Pythagoras from three triangles
line: A 3-4-5 triangle's altitude splits it into two pieces that rotate and flip to line up perfectly with the big one.

title: A parallel line splits sides
line: A line parallel to the base slides up a triangle, and the ratio readouts on the two cut sides stay equal.

title: The bisector's lopsided cut
line: An angle bisector between sides 6 and 4 hits the opposite side and splits it into pieces in a 6:4 ratio.

title: Two angles are enough
line: A small triangle with 50° and 70° angles slides onto a big one's corner and dilates until its third side lands exactly.

title: The third angle comes free
line: A triangle's three corners tear off and line up along a straight line, so fixing two angles forces the third.

title: Is it similar?
line: A shape rotates, flips, and scales by 1.5 to land on its twin, then a stretched copy tries and fails to fit.

title: Ratios lock together
line: Triangles 3-4-5 and 6-8-10 color-match their sides, the ratios 2, 2, 2 count in, and matching angle arcs overlap.

title: Rays from the center
line: A triangle dilates by 2 from a center point, rays through each corner, and each new side stays parallel and doubles.

title: The line that stays put
line: Under a dilation, a line through the center slides along itself, while a line missing the center jumps to a parallel copy.

title: Scaling through zero
line: The scale factor sweeps from 2 to −1, the shape shrinks into the center point, then comes out the other side upside down.

title: Six radii around a circle
line: A compass set to the radius steps around a circle exactly 6 times; the marks join into a hexagon, every other into a triangle.

title: A square from two diameters
line: A diameter is drawn, its perpendicular bisector crosses it, and the four rim points connect into a square inscribed in the circle.

title: Two arcs find the midpoint
line: Arcs swing from both ends of a segment and cross twice, and the line through the crossings cuts it in half at 90°.

title: Copying an angle
line: Compass arcs measure a 40° angle's opening, carry it to a new ray, and a copy appears that overlaps the original exactly.

title: Folding the angle in half
line: One ray of an angle folds onto the other like paper, and the crease left behind is the angle bisector.

title: Diagonals cut each other in half
line: A parallelogram shears and stretches, and its diagonals' four color-matched halves stay equal in pairs the whole time.

title: Half a turn onto itself
line: A parallelogram spins 180° around its center and lands on itself, carrying each side onto its opposite to prove they match.

title: When diagonals become equal
line: A parallelogram's angles tilt toward 90°, and at the exact moment it becomes a rectangle the two diagonal readouts match.

title: Tear off the corners
line: A triangle's three corners snip off and slide together, lining up into a straight 180° line.

title: The midsegment is half
line: A segment joining two side midpoints stays parallel to the base as the triangle reshapes, with a length ratio fixed at 0.5.

title: Medians meet at the balance point
line: Three medians cross at one point that cuts each into a 2:1 split, and the triangle balances there on a pin.

title: Folding an isosceles triangle
line: An isosceles triangle folds along its altitude, the halves overlap exactly, and the base angles land on each other.

title: Vertical angles stay matched
line: Two crossing lines rotate around their meeting point, and the opposite angle readouts change together but always match.

title: Sliding along the transversal
line: An angle at one parallel line slides down the transversal and drops exactly onto its matching angle at the other line.

title: Walking the perpendicular bisector
line: A dot walks along a segment's perpendicular bisector, and its two distance readouts to the segment's ends stay equal.

title: SAS snaps into place
line: A triangle slides, turns, and flips onto one with the same two sides and angle, and its last corner has one place to land.

title: Three sides, two circles
line: Circles of radius 4 and 6 around the ends of a 7-long side cross at two mirror points, so the triangle is fixed.

title: Why SSA fails
line: A side of length 4 swings from an angle of 30° and hits the base line twice, building two different triangles.

title: Landing piece by piece
line: As one triangle slides, turns, and flips onto another, each pair of sides and angles lights up when it lands.

title: Which shape fits
line: An L-shaped tile tries slides, turns, and flips to land on four targets; three fit perfectly and one needs a stretch.

title: Predict the flip
line: A flag shape shows a ghost guess for its reflection across y = x, then actually flips and checks the guess.

title: Three moves to land
line: An arrow shape reaches a target by a slide, a 90° turn, and a flip, each move tracing its path on the grid.

title: Two flips make a turn
line: A shape reflects across two mirror lines that meet at 40°, and the result is the same shape rotated 80°.

title: Two parallel flips make a slide
line: Reflecting a shape across two parallel mirrors 3 units apart slides it 6 units, with no turn at all.

title: Rotation as circles
line: Each corner of a triangle rides its own circle around a center point, sweeping identical 60° arcs.

title: The mirror line as bisector
line: Segments join each point to its reflection, and the mirror line cuts every one at its midpoint at a right angle.

title: Translation as parallel arrows
line: Every point of a shape gets the same arrow, all parallel and equal length, and the shape glides along them.

title: Twelve ways to move a hexagon
line: A hexagon with colored corners runs through 6 rotations and 6 flips, landing on itself each time while a counter climbs to 12.

title: Rectangle versus square
line: A rectangle and a square both try a 90° turn; the square lands on itself, the rectangle sticks out awkwardly.

title: The parallelogram's only trick
line: A parallelogram flips across each diagonal and misses itself, then spins 180° and lands perfectly.

title: Stretch versus slide
line: A circle on a grid slides and stays a circle, then a horizontal stretch squashes it into an ellipse as a ruler readout changes.

title: Points in, points out
line: Points fly through a 90° rotation machine, and a table fills in: (2,1) becomes (−1,2), (3,0) becomes (0,3).

title: A circle is a fixed string
line: A segment of length 2 pinned at one end spins around, and its free end leaves a trail that closes into a circle.
